Creative Work

Ideas into expression

Make an idea connect.

I work with writing, design, and visual storytelling as ways of inviting someone into an idea. I am interested in the choices behind them: what to include, what to leave out, and where to give the reader room.

Start with one person and one thing worth sharing. Use a small planning sheet, follow a guide, or read about the choices behind the work.

One page, one idea

Give the idea a manageable shape.

The blank brief asks who the piece is for, what belongs in it, and what would make it ready enough to share. Use it for a short article, a video, a visual story, or another small piece. Skip the prompts that do not help.

The smallest useful version: name the person, name the idea, and choose the next action. The rest is there when you need it.

Blank template / Plain text

One small creative piece

Reader → idea → material → three beats → finish line.

Includes a permission check and an optional place to define AI assistance. It does not generate a story or collect your answers.

Download the creative brief (.txt)
Read or copy the complete blank brief
ONE SMALL CREATIVE PIECE
A blank planning sheet from Nolan Kido
https://nolankido.com/creative/#creative-brief

Use only the prompts that help. Complete your copy privately.
This is a thinking aid, not a scoring system or a publication checklist.

READER OR VIEWER
Who is this for? What do they already know?

ONE IDEA
What should they understand, notice, or feel?

SMALLEST USEFUL FORM
A short note, a single scene, a few pictures, or another small format:
What belongs in this version? What can wait?

MATERIAL AND PERMISSION
What facts, observations, or source material can I support?
What is uncertain or remembered rather than recorded?
Whose words, image, or story require permission before sharing?
Keep private details and other people's personal material out of public copies.

THREE BEATS
Opening: give the person a reason to care.
Middle: show the detail, change, or example that matters.
Ending: leave them with one clear thought or next step.

OPTIONAL AI ASSISTANCE
What limited help would be useful: organizing, alternatives, or a clarity check?
What must remain in my voice or under my control?
Do not upload private or restricted material without authorization.
Check any suggested facts, quotations, or claims against the source.

READY ENOUGH TO SHARE
What would let the intended person follow this piece?
What factual, permission, or accessibility questions still need resolving?
What is one optional improvement I can leave for another version?

NEXT ACTION
One small action I can take, or a reason to set this aside:

No account is needed. Open the text file in your own notes or text editor and keep the completed copy private. This page has no answer form. Using a cloud notes app or AI service is a separate sharing decision.

This is an AI-assisted planning aid, not a report of a completed personal project. A brief cannot establish permission, verify a fact, or guarantee that a piece will connect.

From reading to making

Choose the kind of piece.

Three practical routes through material already on the site. These are approaches to try, not a portfolio of completed personal projects.

Writing / A first version

Turn a rough idea into something you can share.

Choose a reader, a small scope, and a finish line. Use optional AI assistance without letting it replace the idea you wanted to express.

Work toward: one small version, rather than a growing list of possibilities.

Visual storytelling / A poker-specific guide

From hand note to poker vlog

Follow a poker-specific workflow from recorded action to narration, graphics, and a companion page. Separate what happened from later interpretation.

Work toward: a coherent explanation built from supportable facts. This is a guide, not a published vlog episode.

Personal stories / Someone's voice

Preserve a family story without losing the person's voice.

Start with permission, listen to the speaker, and let them review what you keep. The technology should serve the story.

Work toward: a version the speaker has had a chance to review, not a polished replacement for their voice.
